CVE-2026-58058.title: Nmap through 7.99 does not keep the IPv6 extension-header walk wi ...
CVE-2026-58058.description: Nmap through 7.99 does not keep the IPv6 extension-header walk within the captured packet in ipv6_get_data_primitive (libnetutil/netutil.cc), so the pointer advances past the buffer and the remaining-length computation underflows to a large value. A scanned target or on-path attacker returning a crafted IPv6 response with a truncated extension header can trigger out-of-bounds reads and a crash during raw IPv6 scans.

CVE-2026-72712.title: Nmap versions up to and including 7.99 contains a denial of servi ...
CVE-2026-72712.description: Nmap versions up to and including 7.99 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows remote attackers to crash the application by sending a crafted packet containing a zero-length TCP option. The malformed packet forces the Packet:parse_options() function in nselib/packet.lua to allocate objects in an infinite loop, causing an out-of-memory condition that results in application crash.

CVE-2018-25282.title: nmap: zenmap: Nmap/ZenMap: Denial of Service via XML entity expansion
CVE-2018-25282.description: A flaw was found in Nmap and ZenMap. A local attacker could exploit this vulnerability by crafting a malicious XML file with nested entity definitions. When this file is opened through ZenMap's scan import functionality, it causes the program to consume excessive system resources, leading to a denial of service (DoS) by crashing the application.

CVE-2026-58058.title: nmap: Nmap: Denial of Service via crafted IPv6 response
CVE-2026-58058.description: A flaw was found in Nmap. A remote attacker or a scanned target can send a specially crafted IPv6 response with a truncated extension header. This can lead to an integer underflow, causing out-of-bounds reads and a denial of service (DoS) due to a crash during raw IPv6 scans.

CVE-2026-72712.title: nmap: Nmap: Denial of Service via zero-length TCP option packet
CVE-2026-72712.description: A flaw was found in Nmap. A remote attacker can exploit this denial of service vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet that includes a zero-length Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) option. This malformed packet forces the application to enter an infinite loop during packet processing, consuming excessive memory and ultimately causing the Nmap application to crash.
